provenance_correction.statement: The model below — an always-on depleting poise pool PLUS hyperarmour on declared heavy frames — is ELDEN RING's combination, not DS3's. RI-CMB05's own provenance note cites DS3 exclusively and is simply wrong about which game it copied. This is a CITATION FIX, not a redesign: the model is unchanged and is implemented exactly as written.
provenance_correction.evidence: corpus/10-combat/data/souls-frame-data.json poise.ER.model — 'always-active poise HP pool equal to the visible poise stat; stagger when it reaches 0; resets to max instantly on stagger'. DS3's model is the opposite (hidden 100 poise health, stagger resistable ONLY during active-poise frames).

formula.reset: poise_health := poise_health_max on the frame the stagger animation ENDS

pool.regen_delay_not_rebased: RI-CMB05 §A — authored as a duration (1.500 s), like RI-CMB03's 42 f. A wall-clock condition on the player's behaviour, not an animation length.

stagger.thresholds_not_rebased: The 1-19 / 20-39 / 40-69 / >=70 poise-damage thresholds are quantities of a pool, not frame counts. Only the LENGTHS of the animations they select moved.
rules: No input is accepted during stagger.
Hurtboxes continue to follow the stagger animation's skeleton.

Stagger is NOT cancellable by anything, INCLUDING further hits — a target already staggered takes damage from subsequent hits but the stagger timer does not restart. This is what prevents infinite stunlock and it is a rule, not an optimisation.

hyperarmour._source: RI-CMB05 §C. Windows come from frames.json (RI-CMB02 §B); pools are poise quantities and were NOT rebased.
rules: Inside the window, incoming poise damage depletes the HA pool, not the normal pool. The pool refills instantly when the window ends; a window is not a shared budget across the animation's life.
Hyperarmour prevents STAGGER. It does not prevent DAMAGE. You trade, you win the exchange, and you may still die doing it.
A fully charged R2 multiplies the HA pool by 1.50 and extends the window forward across all charge frames.
Never during startup before the declared window, never during recovery, and never on light attacks except the three two-handed exceptions in frames.json.
Guard break and criticals bypass hyperarmour completely.
Enemies obey the identical rule with their own declared windows. Permanent hyperarmour on an enemy is a design error, not a difficulty setting.

criticals._note: Criticals are GEOMETRY plus STATE. There is no chance component anywhere (ARBITRATION S1, RI-CMB04 §E).

backstab.input: light attack (R1) while all conditions hold on the same frame

parry.stamina_is_flat_by_class: RI-CMB03 §B: "Parry attempt | 22 flat". A per-shield-class parry cost is not authorised by any reference item; the medium shield carried 26 here and in stamina.json §costs.parry_medium_shield, so the number a player with the default loadout actually paid was 26 and not the declared 22 (W1-09 verdict §2.3). Both are now 22. If a class-dependent cost is ever wanted it needs an amendment to RI-CMB03 §B first.
parry.window_map_rule: [a,b] -> [2a-1, 2b], which preserves 1-based inclusive indexing and doubles the length exactly.
parry.upstream_sanity_check: The corpus's recalled Souls parry window of 8-12 t@30 is 267-400 ms. Our rebased windows are 233-400 ms. Before the rebase they were 117-200 ms — half. The rebase lands us on the upstream figure.
parry.no_partial_parry: DS3 has a partial-parry window (a near-miss treated as a normal block). Our corpus has no analogue and this build does not invent one — declared, not silently omitted.
